title: AI-Augmented Scientific Workflow Framework
description: Presents a structured framework for integrating Large Language Models into scientific research workflows while maintaining full human control, accountability, and scientific integrity. Formalizes four core mechanisms—Question Architecture (QA), Entropy Navigation (EN), Reflective Scaffolding (RS), and Strict Separation of Roles (SR)—to support reproducible, transparent, and traceable research.

key_results.main_finding: Formalizes a four-mechanism framework (QA, EN, RS, SR) enabling AI-augmented scientific workflows that preserve full human epistemic authority, reproducibility, and traceability aligned with FAIR principles.

kill_criteria: KC1: Framework fails to maintain traceable provenance—if AI-generated content cannot be reliably distinguished from human-authored content in the workflow, the separation-of-roles mechanism is invalidated.
KC2: Reflective Scaffolding (RS) cannot be grounded in any external formal system (causal model, state machine, schema constraint), rendering the verification layer vacuous.
KC3: Question Architecture (QA) produces no measurable improvement in structuring scientific intent compared to unstructured prompt-based workflows, invalidating the core methodological claim.
KC4: Entropy Navigation (EN) yields no detectable novelty signal above random exploration, removing its justification as a guided search mechanism.
KC5: The Human Validation Gate is routinely bypassed or proves ineffective at catching hallucinated or biased AI outputs in practice, undermining the strict-separation governance model.
